analytical_question: Can both shifts operate a four-week shadow pilot now, and can the retailer sustain routine use?
general_et_finding: An item tag can identify an individual garment during a count; the GS1 case establishes deployment precedent, not local accuracy.
application_finding: Comparing a shadow count of denim with manual recounts can expose stock discrepancies. A tag read alone cannot establish which stock record needs correction.
organization_specific_finding: Sponsorship supported: four-week sponsor commitment. Skills supported for counting: two leads passed exercise. Workflow unknown: off-duty handoff and drill not reported. Infrastructure/data supported for scope: reader, verified tag mapping and barcode fallback. Resources mixed: four weeks funded; recurring funding unknown. Governance supported for corrections: controller approval and no scan writeback. Culture/change partially supported: one reported mismatch without penalty, too little to infer store-wide trust. Operating ownership unknown for closing exceptions; collection roles are known.

evidence.claim: I.T.’S. international used individually tagged garments for inventory counts in apparel stores.
evidence.date_or_recency: GS1 Japan case study, 2012; reviewed November 8, 2026.
evidence.notes: Establishes precedent; no transfer of time savings or present staffing readiness.

evidence.claim: Sponsor funds four weeks of one-store shadow counts. Two shift leads passed a count exercise; staff logged a mismatch without penalty. Stockroom has a reader, verified tag-to-SKU list and barcode recount procedure. Inventory Controller approves ledger corrections after recount; scans cannot write to the ledger. One named floor lead plus a trained deputy can collect counts. Both shifts have reserved count time. The file says nothing about off-duty discrepancy coverage, escalation drills or recurring funding.
evidence.notes: Accepted for the exercise; not audited employer records.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Training and protected count time support a trial but do not establish sustained ownership. The case does not establish value or routine readiness.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence that more information is needed; low confidence about actual coverage.
value_opportunity_implication: Count fully reconciled size/color discrepancies and total staff time, including exception work. Fast scanning alone cannot show operational value.
risk_governance_implication: Keep scans read-only. Escalate unresolved records rather than silently adjusting stock; controller retains correction authority.
recommendation_management_implication: Withhold the two-shift readiness judgment. First, request the accepted closing roster and handoff drill log from store operations. Second, controller should confirm the escalation path; sponsor should document ongoing resource coverage. Until then keep barcode counts authoritative.
change_monitoring_triggers: A roster and successful drill would support pilot readiness; a confirmed unassigned shift would change the conclusion to hold. Revisit before scheduling.
At week four review unresolved cases by shift, recount labor and recurring ownership; send value and adoption tradeoffs to the Adoption Agent.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Who accepts the discrepancy queue when the controller is off duty? Supply named cover, reserved time and a dated drill log. What recurring budget exists?
